_comment: Editor-responsiveness baseline for the Perf trace workflow (.github/workflows/perf-trace.yml). scripts/check-perf-regression.mjs takes the BEST p95 across the workflow's iterations for each scenario and fails if it is more than the threshold percent above `p95_ms` here. Update these numbers in the same commit as a deliberate perf change; this diff is what reviewers see.
_note_provenance: Re-baselined 2026-10-02 from the first CI run of the Perf trace workflow (run 37047471865, ubuntu-latest, best-of-3 p95: typing 38.5, text-to-visual 162.3, visual-sync 7.3, visual-to-text 275.9 ms; the three iterations agreed within 5%). The earlier numbers came from a local container whose headless rendering made typing look ~7x slower than on the runner.
_note_known_cost: Text-to-visual is the 150 ms batching delay plus ~12 ms of incremental work; a full parse (~250 ms on this document) runs only as a fallback or once while idle. Visual-to-text is the 200 ms markdownUpdated debounce plus serialize and the keep-source-style merge.

typing._note: Small absolute numbers: 75% is ~30 ms of headroom for runner jitter.

visual-sync._note: CPU time per visual-pane update; doubles if updates fall back to full parses, which is the regression this guards.
